elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If painful eye with redness, blurred vision, haloes around light, dilated unreactive pupil, headache/nausea/vomiting, acute glaucoma likely. Give acetazolamide 500mg orally, then 250mg 6 hourly.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If gonococcal conjunctivitis likely, give ceftriaxone1 250mg IM and azithromycin 1g orally.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If orbital cellulitis likely, give ceftriaxone 2g IV2/IM. Avoid injecting > 1g IM at one injection site.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If chemical burn: irrigate eye for at least 30 minutes with 1-3 litres sodium chloride 0.9% or sterile water until pH 7.43. If pain, instil 1 drop tetracaine 1% eye drops4 to affected eye. Apply chloramphenicol 1% ointment 6 hourly.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If penetrating/metallic foreign body: avoid removing, cover gently. Avoid lying flat. If deep corneal/scleral injury and transfer delay, instil 1 drop atropine 1% and chloramphenicol 1% ointment.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If pain, give paracetamol 1g 6 hourly.
EYE/VISION SYMPTOMS

1If severe penicillin allergy (previous angioedema, anaphylaxis, urticaria), discuss with doctor. 2Do not mix Ringer's lactate and IV ceftriaxone. 3Place pH band of urine dipstick in the outer corner of eye to test pH after irrigation. 4Strictly avoid giving tetracaine eye drops to patient to take home as they can cause blindness if used too often. 5Common triggers include pollens, household pets, house dust mite, cockroaches and moulds.
Approach to patient with eye/vision symptoms not needing urgent attention
Eyes discharging or watery. Is there a prominent itch? Eyelid problems
• Avoid sharing towels/bedding. Wash hands often. • Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days.
Yes • If both eyes involved or patient has eczema, hayfever or asthma, allergic conjunctivitis likely:
- Help to identify and advise to avoid triggers5. - Give oxymetazoline 0.025% eye drops 1 drop in

each eye 6 hourly up to 7 days. Advise to apply cold compresses. If no better after 7 days: give instead anti-allergy eye drops, sodium cromoglycate 2% 1 drop 6 hourly for 1-3 months or long-term. - If symptoms > 1 month, add cetirizine 10mg once
daily until itch controlled. - If no better or patient wearing contact lenses, refer. - If recurrent nose problem, check for allergic rhinitis

51. If recurrent skin problem, check for urticaria and eczema 82. If recurrent cough or wheeze, check for asthma 138. • If one eye involved and no eczema, hayfever or asthma, localised cause likely: wash eye with sterile water. Try to identify and remove cause. Give oxymetazoline 0.025% eye drops 1 drop 6 hourly for 3 days. If no better after 24 hours, advise to return: refer.

No. Is the discharge clear or pus? • If painful lump on eyelid, stye likely. Apply warm compresses four times a day. Advise to return if no better, discuss. • If itchy/swollen eyelids, wash twice a day with warm water. • Discuss/refer if: - Eyelashes
touching cornea - Eyelids bent
in/out.

Viral conjunctivitis likely • Apply cold compresses. • Give oxymetazoline 0.025% eye drops 1 drop 6 hourly up to 7 days. • Return to work once better/no discharge. • Refer if one red eye for >1 day, or no better after 5 days.
Superficial foreign body

• Wash out eye with sterile water or sodium chloride 0.9%. • If foreign body not visible, use fluorescein stain and ultraviolet light. • Instil 1 drop tetracaine 1% eye drops4 and gently remove foreign body with moist cotton bud. • Apply eye shield until tetracaine has worn off. • Give chloramphenicol 1% ointment 6 hourly in affected eye for 5 days • Refer same day if: - Removal unsuccessful - Damage to eye - Abnormal vision or eye
movement - No better 24 hours after
removal.

Bacterial conjunctivitis likely • Wipe eyes gently from inside to outside with clean cotton wool soaked in sodium chloride 0.9% until pus clears. • Give chloramphenicol 1% ointment 6 hourly in each eye for 7 days. • Return to work after 2 days of treatment and no pus. • Refer if one red eye, or no better after 5 days.
